podcast.title: Aborted Austin City Limits Pilot Performance (1974)
podcast.body: B.W. Stevenson was scheduled to perform for the pilot episode of Austin City Limits alongside Willie Nelson in 1974. His performance was ultimately scrapped due to technical issues and poor publicity leading to a low audience, not because of any fault of his own. Keith Mateland, director of a documentary about Austin City Limits, commented that his success on the pilot would have benefited Stevenson more than the show. "So Stevenson did perform for the pilot episode of Austin City Limits as did Willie Nelson, but according to Bruce Skate, there were some technical issues and there were not a lot of people in the audience for Stevenson's performance."

podcast.title: Later Austin City Limits Appearance (1976)
podcast.body: Although his pilot performance was scrapped, B.W. Stevenson did get another opportunity to perform on Austin City Limits in 1976. However, this appearance did not carry the same weight as being on the pilot during the peak of his hit song "My Maria." "Stevenson did get another opportunity to be on Austin City Limits. He was on in 1976, but you know, it's not the same as being on the pilot when he is still riding the wave of a big hit."

podcast.title: Early Career and Progressive Country (1970s)
podcast.body: B.W. Stevenson was a pioneer of the progressive country movement, alongside artists like Willie Nelson and Jerry Jeff Walker. For a period, he sold shoes during the day and played music at night, suggesting his dedication to his craft despite not yet achieving widespread commercial success as a solo artist. "Like Willie Nelson and Jerry Jeff Walker and others, he was, though, a pioneer of the progressive country movement."

podcast.title: Respected Session Musician
podcast.body: Throughout his career, B.W. Stevenson was highly regarded as a session musician, even if his solo work didn't always achieve commercial success. "He was always well respected as a session musician."
